chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah Musa ibn Yusuf al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid narrated to us, from his father, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Qais al-Rahbi, who said:

I was sitting with Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, at the gate of the palace, until the sun forced him toward the wall of the palace. He hastened to enter, when a man from Hamdan stood up and grabbed his garment, saying: 'O Commander of the Faithful, tell me a comprehensive hadith that God may benefit me by.' He said: 'Were you not in many of our narrations?' He said: 'Yes, but tell me a comprehensive hadith that God may benefit me by.'

He said: 'My beloved, the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, told me: "I shall arrive, I and my Shia, at the Pool quenched and with bright faces, while our enemy shall arrive thirsty and with dark faces." Take this brief from a longer account: you are with the one you love, and for you is what you have acquired. Release me, O brother of Hamdan.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the Shia at the Pool on Judgment Day?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, Imam Ali (AS) relates a concise prophetic tradition to a man from the tribe of Hamdan who seeks a comprehensive teaching. The setting is outside the governor's palace in Kufa, where Ali was sitting until the midday heat compelled him to move inside. The man's insistence on a single all-encompassing saying prompts Ali to quote the Prophet Muhammad (S), who promised that he and his devoted followers (Shia) would arrive at the celestial Pool (al-Hawd) on Judgment Day quenched and radiant, whereas their adversaries would come parched and dark-faced. Ali then distills the teaching into a universally applicable maxim: a person will be reunited with whom they love, and they will reap what they have earned. This hadith was understood by its original audience as a reassurance of the eschatological reward for loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt.
